tags: A real showreel in the first screen
Timecode and a scrub bar on the footage
Jobs that play as you pass
features: A ten second showreel cut from four real clips fills the first screen, with a phone-sized portrait cut for phones
A running timecode and a scrub bar sit on the footage, one segment per job: drag, tap a job or use the arrow keys
Four jobs that play on hover on a laptop and as they come into view on a phone, each one able to jump the reel to its shot
Services set out as a real call sheet, dated next Tuesday with Manchester's sunrise and sunset worked out for that day
Add a line from the sheet and it lands on the request, which comes back as a call sheet with who rings you and when
name: Long Exposure
short: A film company whose first screen is its showreel, with the timecode and scrub bar on top.
long: A four-person production company in black and white, with one red REC dot. The first screen is a showreel cut from four of this year's jobs, with a running timecode and a scrub bar laid over the footage, one segment per job. Below it the four jobs play on hover or as they scroll into view, a still from a night shoot runs edge to edge, and the services are set out as a real call sheet dated next Tuesday. Add a line and it goes straight onto a request that comes back as a call sheet of its own.
proves: A film company's site can open on the film, and still take the enquiry.
story: Film companies tend to bury the reel behind a play button on a black page. This one opens on it, keeps the timecode honest, and lets you scrub straight to the job you care about.
